question.leadin: This man was single-handedly responsible for depressing the price of gold in the Mediterranean region.
question.text: Name this leader who is known for having made an extravagant hajj to Mecca.
question.clue: The architect Abu Isaq al Saheli was commissioned by this ruler to build the Djinguereber mosque.

swap.leadin: Give the following about African Nobel Peace Prize laureates.
swap.text: This South African anti-apartheid leader was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993, three years after he was freed from Robben Island prison and a year before he became South Africa's first freely elected president.
swap.clue: While imprisoned on Robben Island, this person wrote their autobiography Long Walk to Freedom.

question.leadin: This empire was once ruled by Tunka Manin, and its demise brought the rise of the Sosso people.
question.text: Name this empire which had its capital at Koumbi-Saleh and gives its name to a modern day country with capital at Accra.
question.clue: This empire was the first in its region to treat all gold nuggets larger than dust as its king's property.

swap.text: When a hijacked Air France plane landed at this Ugandan airport, Amin supported the hijackers. An ensuing Israeli counterterrorism operation reuslted in the death of Yonatan Netanyahu.
swap.clue: During Idi Amin's reign, members of the PLO were allowed to land a hijacked plane at this airport. Yonatan Netanyahu was killed while rescuing Israeli hostages from this airport in Operation Thunderbolt.

question.leadin: One leader of this country used the Ruvuma Development Association as an example of his policy of ujamaa.
question.text: Name this country, which resulted from the joining of Tanganyika and Zanzibar. Since 1974, this country's official capital has been Dodoma, though many government functions are still based in Dar es Salaam.
question.clue: With its northern neighbor, this country shares the Serengeti Plain, and it borders Lakes Malawi and Tanganyika to the west.

swap.text: This Zulu leader of the early 19th century united several northern tribes to form a consolidated empire.
swap.clue: The iklwa was a shortened version of the assegai promoted by this commander, who was succeeded by Dingane after his assassination.

question.leadin: One ruler of this empire traveled to Mecca to bring back enough mud and timber for a 17-foot pyramidal tomb.
question.text: Name this empire, which was at its greatest height under the rule of Askia Muhammad. This Islamic empire, which used salt as its currency, had its capital at Gao.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.text: The Almoravids, like the Almohads, kept their capital in this modern day country. This country's Rif Region was historically occupied by its northern neighbor.
swap.clue: The 1975 Green March by this nation forced Spain to cede territories, long after it was made a European protectorate through the Treaty of Fez.

question.text: Opoku Ware I and Osei Tutu oversaw the rise of this West African kingdom, whose government consisted of a system of "Big Men," obirempon, who answered to a king crowned on the Golden Stool.
question.clue: The conflict was initiated by the ascension of this polity's King Kofi Karikari in 1867 who had mounted two military expeditions against the Elmina.

swap.leadin: The British defeated the forces of a sultanate on this archipelago in the shortest recorded war.
swap.text: Name this archipelago which the Sultan of Oman seized in 1698. This archipelago later merged with Tanganyika.
swap.clue: Shortly after independence from Britain, John Okello led the revolt that installed Abeid Karume as the leader of this island and its sister island, Pemba.

question.text: Mandela was a member of this political party, which was outlawed following the massacre. After being exiled, it worked with the SACP to engage in guerilla warfare.

swap.leadin: The British opposed the Portuguese Pink Map because it would interfere with this project.
swap.text: Name this project that was envisioned by a political cartoon showing Cecil Rhodes straddling Africa, holding a telegraph line in his hands. This railway project intended to connect British colonies in Africa from north to south.
swap.clue: Land needed for this project was explored by the Pioneer Column after it was acquired in the Rudd Concession, which was obtained from King Lobengula.

question.leadin: Mishake Muyongo led a separatist group active in this region which waged war from 1994 to 1999.
question.text: Name this disputed territory which protrudes eastward from Namibia.
question.clue: This region's namesake Liberation Army failed to force a secession during a 1994-1999 conflict. It was named after Otto von Bismarck's successor as Chancellor of Germany.

swap.text: This name was given to Algerians of French descent who fled the colony and returned to France during and after Algeria's war for independence.
swap.clue: After a week of demonstrations in one capital, the OAS was founded to pursue the goals of this group.

question.leadin: Ritual flogging was a key portion of the yondo ritual that Francois Tombalbaye ("tohm-bahl-BYE") forced his people to undergo as part of a program with this name.
question.text: Give this French-language term also used by Mobutu Sese Seko. This term describes the process of changing personal and place names to reject Western influence.
question.clue: This policy, which also supported the "Three Z's" of "Our Country, Our River, Our Money." This policy renamed the Stanley Pool to the Malebo Pool, amongst other localizations.

swap.leadin: Name these beneficiaries of North African coups.
swap.text: In 1965, this leader of the Algerian military seized control of the country from President Ben Bella. He would rule as Algerian dictator until his 1978 death.

question.leadin: Answer the following about colonial times in British West Africa.
question.text: This style of colonial governance, popularized by Sir Frederick Lugard in Nigeria, allowed pre-colonial tribes and peoples to continue controlling local afairs with a layer of imperial supervision at the top.
question.clue: This policy was codified in a text called Political Memoranda, which dubiously claims it would protect people from "coastal traders" and "Christian Missionaries."

swap.text: This Hutu nationalist militia, whose name means "Those Who Stand Together," killed more than 800,000 people during the Rwandan Civil War.
swap.clue: Most killings during the Rwandan genocide were perpetrated by this Hutu paramilitary group. Leaders of the group like Georges Rutaganda have been convicted of crimes against humanity.

question.leadin: A leader of this movement composed a poem on the death of the colonial police officer Richard Corfield, instructing Corfield on the story he should tell in Hell.
question.text: Name this anti-colonial, pro-Islamic resistance movement in British Somaliland. This movement enacted a short-lived namesake state under the warrior-poet Mohammed Abdallah Hassan, whom the British called the "Mad Mullah."

swap.leadin: One king of this empire had several white Christian missionaries executed in 1885, including Bishop James Hannington, perhaps because they refused to have gay sex with him.
swap.text: Name the empire whose last ruler was that man, Mwanga II, who reached a settlement with the British in 1892.
swap.clue: This kingdom's Kasubi Tombs inter the bisexual king Mwanga II, who executed Christian martyrs and allied with Lord Lugard's protectorate against its former hegemon ("HEDGE-uh-mon") Bunyoro.
